name: Bell 429
summary: Light twin-engine helicopter popular with US air-medical, police and corporate operators, notable for its flat-floor cabin and rear clamshell doors.

wings: Four-blade composite main rotor with a low-profile hub
engines: Two engines side by side on the roof
Two exhausts angled up and aft at the rear of the cowling
fuselage: Deep, rounded cabin with a flat floor and rear clamshell doors under the tail boom
Skids, or retractable wheels on the 429WLG
tail: Four-blade tail rotor made of two offset two-blade sets

tellTales: Light twin with two exhausts, four main blades and an open (not shrouded) tail rotor
Clamshell loading doors under the tail boom

confusedWith.howToTell: The H135 has a shrouded Fenestron tail rotor; the 429 has an open four-blade tail rotor.
The 429 has two engines, two exhausts and a deeper cabin with rear clamshell doors; the 407 has one engine and a 206-style cabin.
The AW109 is slimmer with a pointed nose, retractable wheels and a two-blade tail rotor; the 429 is deeper and usually on skids.
The Bell 427 is smaller and has a more swept cabin; the 429 is larger with a bigger rear cabin.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
